analyst_view.overall: Brest (6th, 18 pts) host Paris FC (2nd, 23 pts) on Friday night after both won last weekend: Brest made it three league wins in a row with a 1-0 at Strasbourg (Edjouma's goal, and goalkeeper Egil Selvik saved a stoppage-time penalty), and Paris FC beat Angers 4-0 to go second. Julien Lachuer's Brest have not conceded in three games, while Liam Rosenior's Paris FC are scoring freely and even rested the league's top scorer, Lassine Sinayoko (9 goals), against Angers, so he should be fresh. Brest are without captain Brendan Chardonnet (calf, no games this season) and Raphael Le Guen (broken leg, out until about January); one Ouest-France report says creative midfielder Kamory Doumbia hurt his ankle and missed Strasbourg, and his status for Friday is not yet known. The site's numbers have no missing players listed for either side, so these absences are not counted, but Chardonnet and Le Guen have been out for weeks and Brest's recent form already reflects that. News was thin four days out (no dedicated preview yet), no referee is named, and nothing pointed clearly either way, so the view stays with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, 1.4 each. Brest have kept three clean sheets in a row and Paris FC have scored 13 in their last six, and the numbers already weigh both of those runs (small momentum and head-to-head moves). Doumbia's possible absence would cost Brest some creativity, but it is only one report so far, so I stay at 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. Brest have won few corners lately (13 in six games) and Paris FC have won plenty (31), and the numbers already move both sides for that form. I found nothing about tactics or lineups that the numbers can't see, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, with Paris FC expected to pick up more (2.4) after 15 cards in their last six games, which the numbers already count. No referee has been named yet and there is no rivalry or stakes angle beyond a top-six game, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.0 shots. Brest have been winning without many chances (at Strasbourg they leaned on long-range efforts), while Paris FC have been shooting more than usual; both trends are already in the numbers' momentum. Sinayoko returning to the Paris FC lineup is the normal picture the numbers assume, so I stay at 24.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Paris FC have hit the target often lately (35 in six), and Brest have allowed few (17), and the numbers already balance those. With news thin and no confirmed lineups, I stay at 8.
